neighbours.label: Arterial blood supply: 'arterial' / 'arteries' / blood 'circulation' in vascular-disease text
fire: Smokers are far more likely to develop peripheral arterial disease in the lower legs.
Fatty deposits harden inside the arteries and slow the flow of blood to the heart.
Cold hands and feet can be a sign of poor arterial circulation in older adults.
The scan showed a narrowing of the arteries that carry blood to the brain.
Walking every day helps patients with peripheral arterial disease to go further without pain.
When the arteries stiffen with age, the heart must push the blood harder.
A clot in one of the leg arteries can cut off the flow of blood within minutes.
Diabetes damages the small arteries and reduces the supply of blood to the feet.
quiet: Smokers are far more likely to develop chronic bronchitis in the lower lungs.
Mineral deposits harden inside the kidneys and slow the flow of urine to the bladder.
Cold hands and feet can be a sign of an underactive thyroid in older adults.
The scan showed a thinning of the bones that support the weight of the spine.
Walking every day helps patients with chronic back pain to go further without rest.
When the joints stiffen with age, the muscles must work harder to move them.
A stone in one of the bile ducts can cut off the flow of bile within hours.
Diabetes damages the small nerves and reduces the sense of touch in the feet.
